reuse.why: Extends the shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend and reuses recurConfigToRSchedule/RSchedule for the new handler, but getDatesInRange writes its own weekend/holiday test instead of the isNonBusinessDay predicate the same diff introduces (left private).

duplication.why: The daily 'skip non-business days' rule is implemented twice (a loop in getNextDate and a flatMap branch in getDatesInRange), and the holiday membership check is re-written inline in getDatesInRange with exact-match only, diverging from the MM-DD handling in isNonBusinessDay.

placement.why: The date-adjustment rule belongs in shared/schedules.ts, yet the daily-vs-other dispatch and holiday test are decided inline in the server handler, while the new handler itself sits correctly next to getUpcomingDates.

scope.why: Changes stay within schedules (shared helper, server handlers, RecurConfig type) and their tests.

maintainability.why: The weekend/holiday decision now lives in three shapes (helper, getNextDate daily loop, getDatesInRange branch) while getUpcomingDates and budget/schedule-template.ts still call the old path without the daily skip or holidays, so the rule already disagrees across call sites.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getDatesInRange decides daily skipping with its own 'd.isWeekend(date) || config.holidays?.includes(...)' instead of a shared predicate; server/budget/schedule-template.ts and getUpcomingDates are not routed through the new daily/holiday rule.

disguised_duplication.where: The non-business-day test in getDatesInRange is a reshaped copy of isNonBusinessDay (Array.includes instead of some/day-or-MM-DD), and the daily-skip branch is reshaped from getNextDate's while-loop into a flatMap filter.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; daily-frequency special cases are added outside it in getNextDate and getDatesInRange; getDatesInRange re-implements the holiday check, and getUpcomingDates plus schedule-template.ts bypass the daily rule.
